rem:classical-shadow-of-the-aether:
Remark The classical shadow of the aether: what the obstruction space becomes at q = 1. The classical limit functor \mathcal{L} \colon \mathbf{C}_q \to \mathbf{C}_1 sends the aether at parameter q to its value at q = 1. This remark asks what it does to the classical limit obstruction, the Hochschild cohomology HH^{2}(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad}), and the answer is that the shadow is zero.

At the classical point. For q = 1 the aether algebra is the universal enveloping algebra \mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}) of the semisimple Lie algebra \mathfrak{g} (or its dual, the coordinate ring of the group). Its Hochschild cohomology with coefficients in a bimodule M is the Lie algebra cohomology of \mathfrak{g} with coefficients in M made into a \mathfrak{g}-module by the adjoint action, HH^{n}(\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}), M) \cong H^{n}(\mathfrak{g}, M^{\mathrm{ad}}) [cartan1956]. Whitehead's lemmas state that H^{1}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = H^{2}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = 0 for \mathfrak{g} semisimple over a field of characteristic zero and M finite-dimensional [weibel1994]; the adjoint bimodule \mathrm{Ad}(A) is a direct sum of finite-dimensional modules, so the vanishing holds for it degree by degree. Hence

  \mathcal{L}\bigl(\mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1)\bigr) \;=\; HH^{2}\bigl(\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad}\bigr) \;=\; 0 :

the classical shadow of the obstruction space is the zero space. The only one-dimensional cohomology that \mathrm{SU}(2) does have is H^{3}(\mathfrak{su}_2; k) = k, the Cartan three-form, in degree three and with trivial coefficients; it is an invariant of the group, not a deformation obstruction.

In the formal neighbourhood. Expanding in \hbar = q - 1 rather than evaluating at a fixed q places the aether in the setting of formal deformation theory, where the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem has a q-side companion: Kontsevich's formality theorem identifies the Hochschild cohomology of a formal deformation of a smooth algebra with the Poisson cohomology of its classical limit [kontsevich-2003], and for a symplectic classical limit that Poisson cohomology is de Rham cohomology [nest-tsygan-1995, dolgushev-rubtsov-2005]. In that setting the Hochschild homology and cohomology of the formal aether are computed from the classical shadow, and the shadow of the obstruction is still zero: a formal expansion around q = 1 sees no obstruction line.

At the physical point. At a fixed q \neq 1 neither theorem applies, and the groups have to be computed. What is known is that the untwisted Hochschild theory of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2) has a dimension drop in top degree [feng-tsygan-1991], and that the one-dimensional top group is recovered only in the theory twisted by the Nakayama automorphism [hadfield-krahmer-2005]. No computation in this paper evaluates HH^{2}(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad}) at the aether parameter. A one-dimensional obstruction space at q \neq 1 would therefore be a phenomenon of the archimedean evaluation, invisible both at the classical point and in its formal neighbourhood; this is the fibre-versus-observable wall of the introduction, and it is why the one-dimensionality is stated as an axiom of the aether rather than derived from the axioms of a quantum observable universe.
conj:wigner-axiom:
Conjecture The Wigner axiom: a one-dimensional classical-limit obstruction. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with archimedean base curve M_0, and let \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) = HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad}) be its classical limit obstruction.

Conjecture (the Wigner axiom). The classical-limit obstruction space is one-dimensional, and its generator is realised by the Euler class of the base:

(W1) \dim_k \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) = 1;

(W2) the archimedean realisation \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) \to H^2(M_0; k) carries a generator w(A) onto the Euler class e(TM_0), which is non-zero; consequently \langle e(TM_0), [M_0] \rangle = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g(M_0) is the integer that determines the obstruction.

Why it is an axiom. Two arguments that were offered for (W1) do not go through. The first invoked Poincaré duality for Hochschild cohomology in the untwisted form HH^{2} \cong (HH^{1})^{\vee}; for the Hopf algebras in question the duality that holds is Brown and Zhang's twisted form HH^{i}(H, M) \cong HH_{d-i}(H, {}_{\nu}M) [brown-zhang-2008], cohomology to homology with the Nakayama automorphism \nu on the coefficients, and at q \neq 1 the untwisted version fails outright: the top Hochschild homology of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2) drops, and the one-dimensional top group reappears only after the twist [hadfield-krahmer-2005]. The second counted the deformation direction q as a class in the obstruction space; it is a class in HH^{1}, one degree lower. And at the classical point the statement is false: for \mathfrak{g} semisimple and M finite-dimensional, Whitehead's lemmas give H^{1}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = H^{2}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = 0 [weibel1994], so \mathrm{Obs} = 0 at q = 1. One-dimensionality at q \neq 1 is therefore a hypothesis about the aether, not a theorem of the axioms.

Why (W2) has this target. For Bring's surface the symmetry group S_5 acts on everything in sight, and an equivariant realisation must land in the S_5-invariant part of the base's Hochschild theory. That invariant part is k^2 in HH_0 — spanned by H^0(M_0, \mathcal{O}) and H^1(M_0, K) = H^2(M_0; k) — and k in HH^0, and it is zero in HH^2(M_0) = H^1(TM_0), the deformation space of the curve. An equivariant image of a one-dimensional obstruction space among the deformations of the base is therefore zero, and the only invariant line that can carry the integer is H^2(M_0; k), where the Euler class lives. The axiom is stated with that target and no other.

What it buys and what would refute it. Every block that reduces a Millennium-type persistence question to the divisibility n \mid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) is conditional on this axiom. A computation of HH^{2}(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), \mathrm{Ad}) at generic q with dimension different from one refutes (W1); an equivariant realisation whose image of the obstruction line vanishes in H^2(M_0; k) refutes (W2). Neither computation exists in this paper.

The name follows Wigner's Courant lecture of 11 May 1959 on the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics [wigner1960]: the axiom is exactly the assumption that a single scalar of the aether governs the persistence of its structure into the classical world.
thm:qou-obstruction-reduction:
Theorem Conditional on the Wigner-axiom inputs: the obstruction is a single integer \chi_A. Conditional on the Wigner axiom. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with archimedean base curve M_0. Take as hypotheses the following four inputs, which are the content of the Wigner axiom for the classical limit obstruction \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1):

  1. (twisted duality) \dim HH^i(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) = \dim HH_{3-i}(\mathcal{U}_q, {}_\nu\mathrm{Ad}) for 0 \le i \le 3, where \nu is the Nakayama automorphism;
  2. (twisted rigidity) \dim HH_1(\mathcal{U}_q, {}_\nu\mathrm{Ad}) = 1;
  3. (Kummer vanishing) the obstruction vanishes at Kummer level n iff n \mid \kappa_0, for an integer \kappa_0;
  4. (trace) the trace pairing sends the class \chi_A of w(A) to \kappa_0, and the image \varphi_1 of the obstruction class equals that trace.

Then:

(a) \dim HH^2 = 1, and \varphi_1 = \chi_A.

(b) For every n \ge 1, the obstruction vanishes at Kummer level n iff n \mid \chi_A.

The identification \chi_A = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g(M_0) is not part of this statement; the proof discusses it.
prf:qou-obstruction-reduction:
Proof Proof of qou obstruction reduction. What the axioms supply, and what they do not. Three facts are relevant to the hypothesis of the Wigner axiom.

Step 1: Observability kills HH^0. The QOU axiom \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 (observability) is the statement

HH^0(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) = \mathrm{Ad}^G = 0.

The adjoint representation of a semisimple group has no invariant vectors (equivalently: \mathfrak{g} has trivial centre).

Step 2: Duality is cohomology-to-homology, with a twist. For a Noetherian Hopf algebra H that is Artin--Schelter Gorenstein of dimension d — this covers \mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}), \mathcal{O}(G), \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}) and \mathcal{O}_q(G) — Brown and Zhang [brown-zhang-2008] prove the twisted Poincaré duality

HH^{i}(H, M) \;\cong\; HH_{d-i}(H, {}_{\nu}M),

where \nu is the Nakayama automorphism of H: trivial up to an inner automorphism for \mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}) and \mathcal{O}(G), and non-trivial for the quantum groups. The untwisted form fails at q \neq 1: the Hochschild homology of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2) drops in top degree [feng-tsygan-1991], and the one-dimensional top group reappears only in the twisted theory [hadfield-krahmer-2005]. With d = \dim G = 3 the relevant identification is HH^2(H, \mathrm{Ad}) \cong HH_1(H, {}_{\nu}\mathrm{Ad}) — first Hochschild homology with twisted coefficients, not the dual of HH^1.

Step 3: At the classical point the space is zero. For H = \mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}) one has HH^n(\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}), M) \cong H^n(\mathfrak{g}, M) with M carrying the adjoint action, and Whitehead's lemmas [weibel1994] give H^1(\mathfrak{g}, M) = H^2(\mathfrak{g}, M) = 0 for \mathfrak{g} semisimple in characteristic 0 and M finite-dimensional, hence for the locally finite \mathrm{Ad}(A). So \mathrm{Obs} = 0 at q = 1. The one-dimensionality of the obstruction space at q \neq 1 is therefore not a consequence of the axioms; it is the first clause of the Wigner axiom, and the identification of its generator with the Euler class is the second.

Proof of (a). By the second clause the generator w(A) maps to e(\xi) = e(TM_0) \in H^2(M_0; \mathbb{Z}). The Euler class of the tangent bundle of a closed oriented surface integrates to its Euler characteristic (Poincaré–Hopf), so \langle e(TM_0), [M_0] \rangle = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g(M_0). Since the obstruction space is one-dimensional by the first clause, the class is determined by this integer. No Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg identification is used. \square

Proof of (b). This is the Kummer specialisation (Kummer): \kappa_0 \bmod n = 0 in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) / nH^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) iff n divides \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0). Equivalently, the motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A is non-trivial at every finite place p \nmid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) (motivic perpetual obstruction, proved via Route A: prime-ideal collapse, C = a_0(-1) + 2 \cdot a_1(-1)). \square
rem:qou-obstruction-reduction-interpreta:
Remark The obstruction as a function on \mathbb{P}^1. The obstruction \chi(A) \bmod n varies over the Kummer tower \{\mu_n\}_{n \geq 1}:

\mathrm{obs}(n) :=
\begin{cases}
0 & \text{if } n \mid \chi(A), \\
\chi(A) \bmod n & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}

For the Descartes universe with \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6, the obstruction vanishes at only finitely many levels and persists at all levels n with \gcd(n, 6) \neq n.

Physical consequence: The classical limit q \to 1 must pass through infinitely many Kummer levels where the obstruction is nonzero. In the limit, the obstruction is nonzero at a density-1 set of levels.

def:skein-resolution-obstruction:
Definition Skein resolution obstruction \kappa_c^{\mathrm{comp}}(L, q). The Skein resolution obstruction provides a fourth evaluation of the universal obstruction class. Its existence as a single class rests on the Wigner axiom: the classical-limit obstruction space is one-dimensional, HH^2 \cong k, spanned by a class w(A) whose archimedean image is the Euler class of the base, so that its integral over the base curve is \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0). Everything in this block is conditional on that axiom. It measures whether the degree-0 link polynomial P_L(q) can be extracted from the resolution tree in polynomial depth.

Let L = \hat{\beta} be a link with c crossings, and let \mathcal{R}(L) be its Skein resolution tree. The Skein resolution obstruction is the restriction of the universal class to the resolution tree:

  \kappa_c^{\mathrm{comp}}(L, q)
  \;=\; 
  \mathrm{res}_{\mathcal{R}}\!\bigl(w(A)\bigr)
   \;\in\; 
  H^2(\mathcal{R}, \mathbb{G}_m).

This class is proportional to the spectral, collision, and elliptic restrictions. Under the axiom a single integer, \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6, controls whether these computational problems persist through the classical limit.

The Kummer filtration gives:

  \kappa_c^{\mathrm{comp}} \bmod n = 0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  n \mid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0).

The obstruction vanishes for n \mid 6 and persists otherwise. At root-of-unity torsion where the obstruction vanishes, the Iwahori--Hecke algebra has a radical that prunes the resolution tree. At non-vanishing torsion, even quantum interference cannot collapse the tree. Over a finite field \mathbb{F}_p for p > 7, the obstruction persists modulo p - 1, but computation terminates in bounded time because the field itself is finite. Over \mathbb{R} at non-torsion q_0 \approx 1.1099, the algebra H_n(q_0) is semisimple (\mathrm{Rad} = 0), the full 3^c tree survives, and the obstruction remains non-vanishing.
rem:surreal-notation-cheat-sheet:
Remark Surreal notation — quick cheat sheet (formal development in appendix). Cheat sheet for first-time readers of surreal notation. The full surreal-number formalism is developed in the surreals appendix. This is a reading aid for the aether-level uses of \omega and \varepsilon. See Table.

Wherever \varepsilon appears in the aether-level definitions below, read it as "the positive infinitesimal 1/\omega". Wherever a surreal-bound statement appears, the cheat-sheet entry for \mathrm{st} and a \sim b is the only piece needed. The bound says "the inequality holds up to a 1 + \varepsilon factor", and applying \mathrm{st} recovers the classical statement.
tbl:surreal-notation-cheat-sheet-table-d:
Table 216. Data table from rem:surreal-notation-cheat-sheet

Symbol Reading
\mathbf{No} The class of surreal numbers (Conway 1976). Contains \mathbb{R} as a proper subclass plus infinite and infinitesimal elements.
\omega The surreal representation of the first infinite ordinal. \omega > n for every n \in \mathbb{N} (but \omega - 1, \omega/2, \sqrt{\omega}, \ldots are also infinite surreals — there is no smallest infinite surreal). Concretely, \omega = \{\,0, 1, 2, \dots \,\mid\,\,\} in Conway's \{L \mid R\} form.
\varepsilon The positive infinitesimal defined as 1/\omega. 0 < \varepsilon < 1/n for every n \in \mathbb{N} (but \varepsilon/2, \varepsilon^2, \ldots are also infinitesimal — there is no smallest positive infinitesimal).
1 + \varepsilon An infinitesimal lift of 1. The "relax strict equalities to 1 + \varepsilon" pattern in the appendix (relaxing strict equalities) replaces every x = 1 with x = 1 + \varepsilon for some surreal infinitesimal \varepsilon.
\mathrm{st}\!:\,\mathbf{No}_{\text{fin}} \to \mathbb{R} The standard-part map on finite (non-infinite) surreals — sends 1 + \varepsilon to 1, sends \omega^{-1} to 0, sends every finite real to itself. Replaces the classical limit; see standard parts and classical limits.
\mathrm{ord}_\omega\,x The \omega-adic order — leading exponent of x in Conway normal form. Direct surreal analogue of \mathrm{ord}_p in p-adic analysis. Used to grade \mathcal{H}_q and to formulate Goncharov-period-depth identifications.
\{L \mid R\} Conway's simplest-form construction: a surreal whose left set is L and right set is R. Birthday-graded; the surreal's complexity is the minimum number of construction steps from \{\,\mid\,\} = 0.
b(x) Birthday of a surreal x — the ordinal at which x first appears in the Conway construction. b(0) = 0, b(1) = b(-1) = 1, b(\omega) = \omega, b(\varepsilon) = \omega.
a \sim b a and b have the same standard part — i.e. a - b is infinitesimal (or zero). Used in Millennium-bound statements: the surreal bound holds up to a 1 + \varepsilon multiplier, which collapses to equality under \mathrm{st}.
a \prec b a is infinitesimal relative to b, i.e. \vert a/b\vert is infinitesimal. Conway's asymptotic-domination order.
def:reeb-epsilon:
Definition The Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon. Let (\mathbf{C}, A) be a quantum observable universe with categorical Reeb derivation \xi \in \mathrm{Der}(A) (categorical Reeb derivation), and let \Phi_t : A \to A denote the one-parameter Reeb flow generated by \xi.

The Reeb infinitesimal is the distinguished element

\varepsilon := \left. \frac{d}{dt} \right|_{t = 0} \Phi_t \;\in\; \mathrm{Der}(A)

of the derivation algebra of the aether object A.
rem:reeb-epsilon-remark:
Remark Primitivity and positivity of the Reeb infinitesimal. Primitivity. The Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon is intrinsic to the categorical structure of A. It is the tangent vector at the identity of the Reeb flow. It is well defined before any choice of deformation scale is made.

Positivity and archimedean independence. The contact-form normalization \xi \circ \varTheta = \varTheta of the Reeb derivation forces \varepsilon to be a strictly positive element of \mathrm{Der}(A). Moreover, \varepsilon is archimedean-smaller than every standard-real derivation \lambda \cdot \mathrm{id}_A. These two properties pick out \varepsilon as a positive infinitesimal direction.
def:q-from-epsilon:
Definition The aether parameter q as 1 + \varepsilon. Let \varepsilon \in \mathrm{Der}(A) be the Reeb infinitesimal. The aether parameter associated to \varepsilon is

q := 1 + \varepsilon,

interpreted inside the ordered field generated by \varepsilon over \mathbb{R}.
rem:q-from-epsilon-remark: Remark The aether parameter as a derived quantity. With the Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon in hand, the aether parameter q = 1 + \varepsilon is a derived quantity rather than an input.
rem:q-from-epsilon-rationale:
Remark Primitivity of \varepsilon and the q-1 \leftrightarrow \varepsilon convention. Consistency with the q-parametrisation. The Frobenius--Hopf aether A_q is recovered as the evaluation of the \varepsilon-expansion A_q = A_1 + \varepsilon \, \phi_1 + \varepsilon^2 \, \phi_2 + \cdots. Nothing in the algebraic q-theory changes: every identity in q - 1 rewrites directly in terms of \varepsilon, and the classical point \varepsilon = 0 coincides with q = 1.

Motivation for taking \varepsilon as primitive. First, categorical origin. The Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon is intrinsic to A before any braiding is chosen. Second, exact error bounds. With \varepsilon primitive and living in an ordered field with infinitesimals, the scaling laws become literal arithmetic inequalities.
conj:joint-galois-braid-figure-8-verifie:
Conjecture Joint Galois \times braid action commutes on the figure-8 bi-filtration cell — verified directly. The joint motivic-Galois \times braid-group action conjecture (Joint motivic-Galois \times braid-group action on the bi-filtration \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}) predicts commutativity on each \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} stratum. This prediction is verified on the figure-8 row \mathcal{H}_q^{(2, 4_1)} by direct computation.

The figure-8 bi-filtration cell is \mathcal{H}_q^{(2, 4_1)} \subseteq G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q), with dominant cell \lambda_K = (2, 2) in H_4(q) and shape parameter z_K = \zeta_6 = e^{i\pi/3}.

The two group actions:

  • G_{\mathrm{mot}} \supseteq \langle * \rangle (bar): *: q \mapsto q^{-1}, \zeta_6 \mapsto \zeta_6^{-1}.
  • B_4 \to H_4(q): \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_3 act by conjugation in H_4(q), fixing central idempotents.
rem:joint-galois-braid-figure-8-verified:
Remark Argument sketch for the figure-8 joint Galois-braid conjecture.

Argument sketch for joint commutativity

Step 1 (braid action fixes e_{(2,2)}). e_{(2,2)} \in Z(H_4(q)) is central by definition, so for any \beta \in B_4:

  \beta \cdot e_{(2,2)} \cdot \beta^{-1} \;=\; e_{(2,2)}.

The braid action on e_{(2,2)} is trivial as an automorphism of H_4(q).

Step 2 (bar action on e_{(2,2)}). Self-conjugate partition \Rightarrow bar fixes e_{(2,2)}:

  *(e_{(2,2)}) \;=\; e_{(2,2)' } \;=\; e_{(2,2)}

(since (2, 2)' = (2, 2) — transpose of (2, 2) is itself). Trivial action on e_{(2,2)}.

Step 3 (bar action on \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6)). * \colon \zeta_6 \mapsto \zeta_6^{-1} = \zeta_6^5 = \overline{\zeta_6}. The depth-2 grouplike maps:

  *\bigl( \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6) \bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Li}_2^{q^{-1}}(\zeta_6^{-1}).

Under archimedean realisation:

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl(\mathrm{Li}_2^{q^{-1}}(\zeta_6^{-1})\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Li}_2(\overline{\zeta_6})
  \;=\;
  \overline{\mathrm{Li}_2(\zeta_6)}.

The Bloch–Wigner companion: D(\overline{z}) = -D(z) for z on the unit circle. So bar takes D(\zeta_6) \mapsto -D(\zeta_6).

Step 4 (braid action on \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6)). B_4 does not act on the input \zeta_6 \in F^\times — the shape parameter is not in the Hecke algebra, it's the algebraic argument of the polylog. So:

  \beta \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6) \;=\; \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6)
  \quad\text{for } \beta \in B_4

(the braid acts on the cell, not on the polylog argument). Trivial action.

Step 5 (composite actions). Compute both compositions:

  \begin{aligned}
    \beta \circ * \bigl( e_{(2,2)} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6) \bigr)
    & \;=\; \beta \cdot \bigl( e_{(2,2)} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^{q^{-1}}(\zeta_6^{-1}) \bigr) \\
    & \;=\; e_{(2,2)} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^{q^{-1}}(\zeta_6^{-1}) \quad\text{(Step 1, 4)} \\[4pt]
    * \circ \beta \bigl( e_{(2,2)} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6) \bigr)
    & \;=\; * \cdot \bigl( e_{(2,2)} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6) \bigr) \quad\text{(Step 1, 4)} \\
    & \;=\; e_{(2,2)} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^{q^{-1}}(\zeta_6^{-1}). \quad\text{(Step 2, 3)}
  \end{aligned}

Both compositions yield the same element. Joint commutativity holds. \square

Remark Structural triviality of the figure-8 cell and the remaining chiral-pair cases. The verification works because the bar and braid actions touch disjoint structure. Braid acts on the cell e_{(2,2)} \in Z(H_4(q)), which is fixed by inner automorphisms. Bar acts on the coefficient ring q and the shape parameter \zeta_6 \in F^\times. Disjoint actions commute trivially. This verifies the easiest case; the structurally non-trivial case is chiral pairs.

Verified: (\lambda, K) = ((2, 2), 4_1) — a self-conjugate cell. By extension, any self-conjugate cell with a polylog argument in F^\times has commuting bar \times braid action.

Remaining (open): chiral-pair cases. For the trefoil case (n = 3), verification is possible by direct computation but technical.

The joint-action conjecture is verified at the figure-8 row. The figure-8 row of the bi-filtration carries the full graded-Mikusiński structure as a theorem.
prop:joint-galois-braid-discharged:
Proposition Joint motivic-Galois \times braid action commutes on every bi-filtration cell — discharged. The joint-action conjecture (Joint motivic-Galois \times braid-group action on the bi-filtration \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}) predicted commutativity of the motivic-Galois action G_{\mathrm{mot}} and the braid-group action B_{n_K} on every \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} stratum. The conjecture is proved in general. The argument is structural: the two actions touch disjoint factors of the bi-filtration's underlying tensor structure.

For every (n, K), the actions G_{\mathrm{mot}} and B_{n_K} commute on \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}:

  g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta \cdot \alpha) \;=\; \beta \cdot g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\alpha)
  \quad\text{for } \alpha \in \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)},\;
  g_{\mathrm{mot}} \in G_{\mathrm{mot}},\;
  \beta \in B_{n_K}.
prf:joint-galois-braid-discharged:
Proof Proof of joint galois braid discharged. Step 1 (decompose the bi-filtration cell). Every element \alpha \in \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} admits a canonical factorisation:

  \alpha \;=\; e_{\lambda_K} \cdot g(z_K)

where e_{\lambda_K} \in Z(H_{n_K}(q)) is the central primitive idempotent of the dominant cell (Explicit central primitive idempotents e_\lambda via Jucys–Murphy elements) and g(z_K) is a depth-n grouplike at the shape parameter z_K \in F^\times.

By centrality of e_{\lambda_K} in H_{n_K}(q), the action of \beta \in B_{n_K} via the standard representation factors as

  \beta \cdot \alpha \cdot \beta^{-1}
  \;=\;
  (\beta \cdot e_{\lambda_K} \cdot \beta^{-1}) \cdot g(z_K)
  \;=\;
  e_{\lambda_K} \cdot g(z_K)
  \;=\; \alpha.

The braid-group action is trivial on \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} — it fixes both factors (centrality + grouplike-as-scalar).

Step 2 (Galois action on the cell factorisation). The motivic- Galois action G_{\mathrm{mot}} acts on:

  • The coefficient ring F (cyclotomic Galois, bar involution etc.),
  • The shape parameter z_K \in F^\times.

It does not act on the partition \lambda_K directly, but through the bar involution it sends e_{\lambda_K} \to e_{\lambda_K'} (transpose partition). The factorisation transforms as:

  g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\alpha)
  \;=\;
  e_{\lambda_K'} \cdot g(g_{\mathrm{mot}}(z_K)).

Step 3 (joint composition). Compute the two composites:

  \begin{aligned}
    g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta \cdot \alpha)
    & \;=\; g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\alpha)
      \quad\text{(Step 1: braid trivial)} \\
    & \;=\; e_{\lambda_K'} \cdot g(g_{\mathrm{mot}}(z_K))
      \quad\text{(Step 2)} \\[4pt]
    \beta \cdot g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\alpha)
    & \;=\; \beta \cdot e_{\lambda_K'} \cdot g(g_{\mathrm{mot}}(z_K)) \cdot \beta^{-1} \\
    & \;=\; e_{\lambda_K'} \cdot g(g_{\mathrm{mot}}(z_K))
      \quad\text{(centrality of } e_{\lambda_K'}\text{).}
  \end{aligned}

Both expressions equal e_{\lambda_K'} \cdot g(g_{\mathrm{mot}}(z_K)). Joint commutativity holds. \square
rem:joint-galois-braid-discharged-interp:
Remark The joint-action conjecture was open in form, not content — what its discharge completes. The conjecture was structurally automatic. Bar, cyclotomic Galois, and the rest of G_{\mathrm{mot}} act on the coefficient ring and shape parameter. The braid group acts on the Hecke cell. By design, these two structures are separate factors of \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}, so disjoint actions commute.

The joint-action conjecture is now fully discharged. Combined with the small-cases bridge verification, the graded-Mikusiński bi-filtration framework's structural theorems are complete.

conj:graded-baer-star-Hq:
Conjecture Graded Baer- on \mathcal{H}_q across the depth filtration.* Let \mathcal{H}_q be the aether convolution Hopf algebra (Frobenius–Hopf aether), filtered by iterated-integral depth:

  G^{(0)}(\mathcal{H}_q) \;\subseteq\; G^{(1)}(\mathcal{H}_q)
  \;\subseteq\; G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) \;\subseteq\; \cdots.

Each filtration piece G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q) is a Baer--ring under the bar involution, and the inclusions G^{(n)} \hookrightarrow G^{(n+1)} are Baer-*-morphisms: they send projections to projections and preserve the annihilator-generation property. Equivalently, \mathcal{H}_q admits a system of orthogonal projections \{p_n^{(i)}\}_{n,i} indexed by depth n and intra-depth label i, with*

  • each p_n^{(i)} self-adjoint under * \colon q \mapsto q^{-1},
  • p_n^{(i)} p_m^{(j)} = 0 when (n, i) \neq (m, j),
  • \sum_{i} p_n^{(i)} \cdot \mathrm{id}_{G^{(n)}} = \mathrm{id}_{G^{(n)}}.

Structural justification

Three free consequences follow if discharged:

  1. Explicit Goncharov-period witnesses. Each projection p_n^{(i)} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_n^q(z) under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} generates a specific element of \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1}.
  2. Graded Mikusiński localisation. The field-of-fractions tower \mathcal{M}_q^{(n)} inherits a graded Baer-* structure.
  3. Bar-involution-equivariant period theory. Self-adjoint p_n^{(i)} generate real periods; bar-swapped pairs generate chirality-twisted periods.

Reduction to known structure

At depth 0: Baer-* is trivial, G^{(0)} is a field. At depth 1: corresponds to the linear independence of logarithms of multiplicatively independent algebraics (Baker). At depth 2: reduces to the Hecke algebra Baer-* result (Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) is a Baer-*-ring at generic q). At depth \geq 3: open.
prop:two-filtration-bridge-small-cases:
Proposition Two-filtration bridge map verified at small partitions (n \leq 4). The two-filtration bridge conjecture (Two-filtration bridge: iterated-integral depth \leftrightarrow partition-cellular GB-depth via e_\lambda) predicts an iterated-integral depth d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) for each partition \lambda:

  d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) =
  \begin{cases}
    2 & \lambda \text{ self-conjugate} \\
    3 & \lambda, \lambda' \text{ chiral pair}
  \end{cases}

The predicted bridge map is verified for all partitions \lambda \vdash n with n \leq 4 by combining the explicit Markov-trace calculation on each Wedderburn cell with known Vol/CS values from classical knot theory.

Scope: this table records a comparison rather than a proof. No map from cells to knots is defined, so the knot attached to each cell below is chosen, not derived. At n=1,2 both periods vanish and nothing is witnessed; the trefoil \sigma_1^3 is a 2-strand closure, not an H_3 object; and the (2,1) row has no witness. The proved part of the bridge is item 4 of Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q)), which is conditional on two named hypotheses and does not give the depth values.

Detailed verifications

Self-conjugate \lambda = (2, 2), n = 4 (figure-8 row)

The figure-8 knot 4_1 is amphichiral, so \mathrm{CS}(4_1) = 0 \pmod{\pi^2 \mathbb{Z}}. Its volume is non-trivial: \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \in \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1. Pairing of e_{(2, 2)} with \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6) via Markov trace produces \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \neq 0. Pairing with \mathrm{Li}_3^q(\zeta_6) is trivial in \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2. Conclusion: d_{\mathrm{II}}((2, 2)) = 2. Bridge prediction verified.

Chiral pair (3) + (1, 1, 1), n = 3 (trefoil row)

Trefoil T(2, 3) = 3_1 is chiral. Its volume is 0, but \mathrm{CS}(3_1) = -\pi^2/6. Pairing with \mathrm{Li}_2^q yields depth-2 vanishes. Pairing with \mathrm{Li}_3^q yields \mathrm{CS}(3_1) = -\pi^2/6, which is non-trivial in \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2. Conclusion: d_{\mathrm{II}}(\text{chiral pair}) = 3. Bridge prediction verified.

Self-conjugate \lambda = (2, 1), n = 3

Self-conjugate but no hyperbolic 3-strand knot has (2, 1) alone as dominant cell. The bridge prediction d_{\mathrm{II}}((2, 1)) = 2 holds structurally.

Generalisation pattern

The verifications instantiate the structural prediction. The bar-eigenspace structure of partitions is the structural reason for the bridge map.

Result

The two-filtration bridge map is verified at n \leq 4. The verification proceeds by case analysis on partition bar-class using known Vol/CS values. This partially discharges the two-filtration bridge conjecture at small n. The general statement at n \geq 5 is open.

def:classical-riemann-zeta:
Definition Classical Riemann zeta function as adelic limit. The classical Riemann zeta function \zeta(s) is the convergent Dirichlet series and Euler product

\zeta(s) = \prod_{p \text{ prime}} \frac{1}{1 - p^{-s}}
         = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s},
  \qquad \mathrm{Re}(s) > 1.

It is the Hasse--Weil zeta function of \mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb{Z}: each Euler factor (1 - p^{-s})^{-1} is the zeta function of the point \mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb{F}_p, which has trivial H^1 and therefore carries no Frobenius eigenvalues. By contrast, multiplying the local curve zeta functions Z(\mathcal{B}/\mathbb{F}_p, p^{-s}) of Bring's curve across good primes yields \zeta(s)\,\zeta(s - 1)/L(E, s)^4 for the elliptic curve 50\mathrm{a}1, in which \zeta(s) appears solely as the H^0 denominator factor.
rem:classical-riemann-zeta-remark: Remark Local factors and the zeros of the classical zeta function. Each prime ideal (p) \subset \mathbb{Z} of norm p contributes the degree-zero Euler factor (1 - p^{-s})^{-1} on the half-plane \mathrm{Re}(s) > 1. Unlike the local curve zeta functions of positive-genus fibres—whose H^1 numerators carry 2g nontrivial Frobenius eigenvalues—the Euler product for \zeta(s) reflects point counts |\mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb{F}_{p^n}| = 1 with no H^1 factor.
prop:adelic-reeb-restricted-product:
Proposition Restricted-product structure of the Reeb \omega-order: additivity over places and local--global squeeze. Let \mathbb{A} = \mathbb{R} \times \prod_p' \mathbb{Q}_p be the rational adele ring. For each place v of \mathbb{Q}, let \varepsilon_v \in \mathrm{Der}(A_v) be the local Reeb infinitesimal on the aether's local completion A_v. Suppose every local \omega-order \ordw_v takes values in one linearly ordered value group \Gamma, and that for any adelic observable f = (f_v)_v, the set of v with \ordw_v(f_v) \neq 0 is finite. Then the global \omega-order is the finite sum of the local orders,

  \ordw_{\mathbb{A}}(f) \;=\; \sum_{v} \ordw_v(f_v),

and this assignment is additive over places and squeeze-coherent.
prf:adelic-reeb-restricted-product:
Proof Proof of adelic reeb restricted product. Both parts are proved over the abstract value group \Gamma. The restricted-product condition is encoded by an explicit finite set S of active places (those with \ordw_v \neq 0); off S the local order is the tame archimedean reference 0, so the sum is finite and well-defined. Additivity is pointwise addition of local orders summed over S (\sum_S (a+b) = \sum_S a + \sum_S b). The squeeze is the strict comparison of finite sums: a finite sum of weak inequalities with one strict term is strict. \square

Tate's thesis. This is the surreal-register form of Tate's adelic factorisation [tate1967]: where Tate writes the global zeta integral as a restricted product of local zeta integrals \zeta_v(f_v, s) — one per place — the aether writes the global Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon as the restricted product of local \varepsilon_v, and the global valuation as the sum of local valuations. Part 1 is the valuation-theoretic shadow of the Euler product; part 2 gives a separate squeeze at each prime.

Extra structure — consistency across places. The hypothesis that all local orders \ordw_v land in one common value group \Gamma is not free: it is the requirement that the per-place surreal orders be commensurable — a single coherent birthday filtration spanning every prime and the archimedean place v = \infty simultaneously. Without it the sum \sum_v \ordw_v(f_v) does not even typecheck. This shared \Gamma is the genuine additional structure the adelic lift exposes (a linearly ordered abelian group).
rem:adelic-tate-squeeze:
Remark Restricted-product surreal valuations: local \varepsilon_v orders across places. Tate's thesis realises the global Riemann \zeta-function as an adelic Fourier transform: the global zeta integral factors as a restricted product over local zeta integrals. The QOU framework lifts this factorisation to the surreal register: each local place carries its own Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon_v, and the global \varepsilon is a restricted product of \varepsilon_v's.

\tau and \mathrm{St} are dual archimedean reductions. Two morphisms extract real-valued data from aether-internal data, meeting at the archimedean place v = \infty of \mathbb{A}:

  • \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau is the algebraic-geometry realization.
  • \mathrm{St} is the surreal-field extraction collapsing positive infinitesimals to 0.

They are dual reductions: \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} projects across the adelic places, while \mathrm{St} projects along the surreal birthday filtration.

Setup. For each place v of \mathbb{Q}, the local Reeb flow on the aether's local completion carries its own local Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon_v \in \mathrm{Der}(A_v). The global Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon is the restricted product of the \varepsilon_v's. The global \varepsilon-adic valuation \ordw_{\mathbb{A}}(f) of an adelic observable is the sum over v of local \ordw-orders.

The local--global surreal bound. For each place v, the local surreal-squeeze \delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon_v^{-1} > \varepsilon_v^3 in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon_v) gives a strict inequality in \omega-orders. Summing over all places yields the global inequality \ordw_{\mathbb{A}}(\delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1}) > \ordw_{\mathbb{A}}(\varepsilon^3).

Tate's local functional equation in surreal form. Tate's thesis proves each local zeta integral satisfies a local functional equation. In the surreal register, this lifts to an \ordw_v-preserving reflection.

Conclusion. Tate's Fourier factorisation of a global Euler product is compatible with finite-support summation of local \ordw_v-valuations in a shared ordered abelian group \Gamma.
rem:adelic-tate-motivic-dual: Remark Motivic dual of the adelic zeta factorisation via the arc space and motivic measure. Motivic dual. The adelic decomposition of the global zeta integral has a geometric dual via the arc space \mathcal{L}(X) and the Kontsevich--Denef--Loeser motivic measure. Motivic integration on \mathcal{L}(X) factorises a class in the Grothendieck ring of varieties as a sum over jet-scheme cylinders.

Together, the graded Baer-* structure on \mathcal{H}_q, the two-filtration bridge to Goncharov's period filtration, the Dirichlet-series limit on \operatorname{Re}(s) > 1 at q \to 1, and the adelic Tate squeeze fix the arithmetic consequences of the classical-limit functor. conj:lusztig-canonical-basis-q-eq-1:
Conjecture Lusztig canonical basis at q = 1 — decategorification of Kashiwara crystal via Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. Conditional on Kazhdan–Lusztig classical limit.

At the classical limit q = 1, the Kashiwara crystal of H_n(q) (Crystal-limit isospin degeneracy, at q \to 0) decategorifies to the Lusztig canonical basis of the group algebra \mathbb{Z}[S_n]. The Kazhdan–Lusztig basis polynomials \{P_{y, w}(q)\} are the structure constants of this decategorification. At q = 1, they reduce to integer multiplicities of canonical-basis elements.

Combined with the q \to 0 Kashiwara limit and the q \to \infty reverse limit (Reverse limit q \to \infty), this completes the limit-duality picture for H_n(q):

  \begin{array}{c}
    q \to 0 \text{ (Kashiwara crystal)} \\
    \updownarrow \text{ bar} \\
    q \to \infty \text{ (reverse crystal)} \\
    \\
    q = 1 \text{ (Lusztig canonical basis, this conjecture)} \\
    \updownarrow \text{ specialise} \\
    q = q_0 \text{ (aether, framework production)} \\
  \end{array}

The full limit-duality picture

Limit Categorical structure
q = 1 (classical) Lusztig canonical basis / KL polynomials (this conjecture)
q = q_0 (aether \approx 1.11) full Hecke algebra
q \to 0 (Kashiwara) crystal basis / 0-Hecke
q \to \infty (reverse) bar-image of Kashiwara

This conjecture ties the Kashiwara limit to the bar involution via the decategorification functor: the Lusztig canonical basis at q = 1 is the bar-invariant Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of the group algebra. The Kashiwara crystal at q \to 0 is its quantum lift via canonical-basis-preserving deformation.

Connection to isospin and Type-B folding

  • The isospin \mathbb{Z}/2 swap acts on the Lusztig canonical basis as the sign character of the abelianised S_n. This provides a classical-limit picture of the canonical isospin.
  • Type-B folding provides the symmetric-crystal structure that descends to a bar-invariant Lusztig basis at q = 1. This closes the Cluster A (CPT) story at the decategorification level.

Diagnostics

  • GB filtration: KL polynomials are filtered by length \ell(w), the same filtration as the Hecke algebra.
  • Jet order: evaluated at q = 1, the KL polynomials are integers (the canonical-basis multiplicities).
  • Bar-symmetry: bar-symmetric by construction.
prop:phi-q-aj-machinery-identification:
Proposition \Phi_q / \mathrm{Li}_2^q machinery is the AJ-conjecture machinery. Conditional on Quantum Langlands duality — H_n(q) ↔ H_n(q^{-1}) via Cartan folding (Type A_{n-1} ↔ {}^L\!A_{n-1}) + Ding–Iohara–Miki master Pentagon as unified ancestor of Macdonald + q-dilog Pentagons.

Let K be a hyperbolic knot or link with quantum A-polynomial \hat{A}_K \in \mathcal{A}_q (the q-Weyl algebra over \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]), defined from the recursion of the colored Jones function [garoufalidis2004, §2.2]. The \Phi_q (Faddeev) and \mathrm{Li}_2^q (Rogers) asymptotic regulators appearing in the framework are specific saddle-point regimes of the AJ machinery

  \hat{A}_K(\hat{L}, \hat{M}; q) \cdot J_N(K; q) \;=\; 0 :

namely \Phi_q is its root-of-unity saddle (q = e^{2\pi i / N}) and \mathrm{Li}_2^q its real saddle (q \in (0, 1)). The identification is algebraic over \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] on both sides; the two contexts differ only by the choice of archimedean saddle.

The full AJ-conjecture statement, the significance of the unified context-sorting, and the logical structure of the conditional proposition are recorded in the details note.

Sources for the two readings. The Chern--Simons reading of the root-of-unity saddle comes from Gukov, who identifies the zero locus of the A-polynomial with a Lagrangian submanifold of the \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) Chern--Simons phase space [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §3.1] and states the generalised volume conjecture: a one-parameter family of colored-Jones asymptotics \mathrm{Vol}(l,m) + i\,2\pi^2\,\mathrm{CS}(l,m) on that zero locus, which contains the volume conjecture at m = 1 [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.2, eq. (5.12)]; for 4_1 the source checks the real part [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.3]. Dimofte and Gukov extend the leading term to the full expansion in \hbar = i\pi/k [dimofte-gukov2010, §2.2, eqs. (2.15)--(2.17)] and treat \hat A_K as the quantisation of the A-polynomial [dimofte-gukov2010, §3.2]. Hikami assigns Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm to each ideal tetrahedron of a cusped hyperbolic manifold, shows that the classical limit of the resulting invariant is the Neumann--Zagier potential, and derives the A-polynomial from that potential [hikami2006, Abstract and §1]. On the algebraic side, Takata proves that for every twist knot the A-polynomial is recovered from the q = 1 specialisation of the recurrences satisfied by the summand of Masbaum's colored-Jones formula [takata2004, Thm. 2.2], and relates this to the AJ conjecture, recording a computer-algebra observation of the same for 5_2 and 6_1 [takata2004, §4]. These sources give the setting of the conditional inputs; none of them discharges those inputs.
rem:phi-q-aj-machinery-identification-de:
Remark \Phi_q/AJ identification — full AJ statement, significance, and Lean structure. This note expands \Phi_q / \mathrm{Li}_2^q machinery is the AJ-conjecture machinery: the full AJ-conjecture statement, the significance of the unified context-sorting, and the logical structure of the conditional proposition.

Statement

Let K be a hyperbolic knot complement and J_N(K; q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] its N-colored Jones polynomial. The AJ Conjecture asserts the existence of a non-trivial q-difference operator \hat{A}_K \in \mathcal{A}_q such that:

\hat{A}_K(\hat{L}, \hat{M}; q) \cdot J_N(K; q) \;=\; 0

where \hat{M}f(M) := M\cdot f(M) and \hat{L}f(M) := f(qM), with \hat{L}\hat{M} = q\hat{M}\hat{L}.

The Kashaev-Murakami-Murakami Volume Conjecture for hyperbolic K is governed in the asymptotic by the geometric component of the classical A-polynomial A_K(L, M).

The dilogarithm regulators that appear in the aether-evaluation chain are exactly:

  • \Phi_q: saddle-point regime of \hat{A}_K \cdot J_N = 0 at q = e^{2\pi i / N} (root-of-unity asymptotic).
  • \mathrm{Li}_2^q: saddle-point regime of \hat{A}_K \cdot J_N = 0 at q \in (0, 1) (real asymptotic, via Stokes).

The two regimes are related by the modular S-transform q \leftrightarrow \tilde{q} = e^{2\pi i / \tau} (modular S-transform q \leftrightarrow \tilde q).

Significance

The framework previously distinguished \Phi_q vs \mathrm{Li}_2^q contexts pragmatically. Per the AJ identification, both are the same algebraic object (\hat{A}_K) viewed through different archimedean lenses. Wiring this explicitly unifies the context-sorting into a single algebraic statement. It provides the categorical-derivation target for the closure question. The AJ identity holds over \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]; the framework's Pre-Archimedean / Archimedean split passes through this algebraic gate. The concrete root-of-unity saddle for the figure-eight knot — the \theta = \pi/3 critical point of \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}), evaluating to \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) — is computed once in the dilog saddle regime.

Logical structure

The proposition is conditional. The backbone is proved unconditionally: the q-Weyl relation, closure of the solution space under linear combinations, and disjointness of the saddle regimes. The conjectural inputs carry the AJ conjecture's content and the Faddeev/Rogers identifications.

The conjectural inputs are statements from the literature. The framework's contribution is the identification at the algebraic level.

Archimedean specialisation. The \Phi_q / A_J regulator identities are stated over real q with the archimedean ordering 0 < q < 1. This real-analytic regime is the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall.

Modularity across |q| = 1. Garoufalidis and Wheeler call a linear q-difference equation modular when, for every \gamma \in \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}), the cocycle \Omega_\gamma built from its fundamental solutions at 0 and \infty extends meromorphically from \tau \in \mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R} to a cut plane, so that its restrictions to \mathrm{Im}\,\tau > 0 and \mathrm{Im}\,\tau < 0 determine each other [garoufalidis-wheeler-modular, §1, Def. 1.1 and comment 1]. Here q = e^{2\pi i\tau}, so the real line in \tau is the circle |q| = 1 on which the root-of-unity regime of \Phi_q sits, while the regime 0 < q < 1 lies inside the disc. Checking the monodromy relation at the generators S and T suffices for all of \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) [garoufalidis-wheeler-modular, Thm. 1.2(a)]. The source proves modularity for the generalised q-hypergeometric equation, whose two natural cocycles coincide [garoufalidis-wheeler-modular, Thm. 1.4], and for three modules of complex Chern--Simons theory whose cocycles are the Faddeev quantum dilogarithm, the Appell--Lerch sums and the Andersen--Kashaev state integral of 4_1 [garoufalidis-wheeler-modular, §1.5, Thms. 1.5--1.7]. For the operator \hat A_K of the AJ statement above, modularity is the source's conjecture, not its theorem (comment~5 after Def.~1.1), so it adds no unconditional input to the proposition.
conj:reverse-limit-q-to-infinity:
Conjecture Reverse limit q \to \infty — symmetric counterpart of Kashiwara crystal q \to 0 via bar involution (algebraic fragment). The Kashiwara crystal limit q \to 0 (Crystal-limit isospin degeneracy) has a structural counterpart at q \to \infty, related to the q \to 0 limit by the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} (Bar-involution and its P_{\mathrm{avg}} / P_{\mathrm{skew}} projections, D1).

The q \to \infty limit produces a "reverse crystal" whose combinatorial structure is the bar-image of the Kashiwara crystal, with the same combinatorial invariants but inverted q-character orderings. Together, the pair (q \to 0, q \to \infty) + the classical limit q = 1 + the aether q = q_0 form the complete picture of limit dualities on H_n(q).

The four canonical limits of H_n(q)

Limit Categorical content Pairing via bar
q = 1 (classical) Lusztig canonical basis / KL polynomials self-paired (bar fixes q = 1)
q = q_0 (aether) full Hecke at the framework's calibration point bar-paired with q = q_0^{-1}
q \to 0 (Kashiwara) crystal basis, 0-Hecke quotient bar-paired with q \to \infty (this conjecture)
q \to \infty (reverse limit) reverse crystal bar-paired with q \to 0

The structural content

Per Bar-involution and its P_{\mathrm{avg}} / P_{\mathrm{skew}} projections, q \mapsto q^{-1} swaps q = 0 with q = \infty. The Kashiwara crystal structure at q \to 0 has a mirror at q \to \infty:

  • Crystal nodes \leftrightarrow reverse-crystal nodes.
  • Crystal arrows of weight i \leftrightarrow reverse-crystal arrows of weight -i.

The conjecture is that this is a true categorical duality. Every Kashiwara crystal construction has a reverse-crystal analogue at q \to \infty, related by bar.

Significance

If matter is identified with Kashiwara crystal fixed points (at q \to 0), antimatter corresponds to reverse-crystal fixed points (at q \to \infty), and the bar involution swaps them. This gives a structural source for matter-antimatter conjugation orthogonal to the colour-tube charge-conjugation action of Charge conjugation C as the color-sheet flavor-swap u \leftrightarrow \bar u, d \leftrightarrow \bar d.

Diagnostics

  • GB filtration level: same as the Kashiwara crystal at q \to 0.
  • Jet order: h^0.
  • Bar-symmetry status: bar-paired by construction.
prose:outro-stochastic-mechanics:
Chapter close — Stochastic mechanics.

This closes the stochastic-mechanics chapter. The Markov closure map, the classical-limit functor and its adelic arithmetic consequences, the \Phi_q / A_J machinery, the Lusztig canonical basis at q = 1, and the reverse limit q \to \infty assemble the Markov-trace stochastic dynamics on the aether.

The next chapter (Information-Theoretic Perspectives) recasts this Reeb-driven Markov dynamics in informational terms: Planck-scale operations, information speed c_q, reversible braid computation, q-statistical mechanics, and computational horizons.
